newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Language delays Colombia ruling on seized Britons.
newsitem.headline: Language delays Colombia ruling on seized Britons.

text.p: Three Britons being held on charges of trying to smuggle $50 million cocaine out of Colombia were unable to give evidence to prosecutors Monday as planned because of problems finding an interpreter, an official said.

Michael Hayne, 50, of Egham, Surrey, his son Stephen Alan Hayne, 27, of Ashford, Kent, and David Maurice Shaw, 49, of Oldham were arrested Friday evening in the Caribbean coastal port of Barranquilla.

A spokesman for the DAS state security agency alleged that its agents found more than 425 pounds (194 kg) of high grade cocaine when they searched the luxury U.S.-registered yacht Perla del Mar, in which they were travelling.

"The men have been unable to answer prosecutors' questions or give other evidence because the British consul has been unable to find them a translator and none of them speaks a word of Spanish," a spokeswoman for the regional prosecutor's office in Barranquilla said.
British diplomatic sources in Barranquilla said the men were "frightened and shocked" by their experience.
In a weekend phone interview from jail, Michael Hayne told Reuters the arrest had been a "huge mix-up" and he hoped things would soon be "straightened out."
He said conditions in the jail where the trio are in custody were fine and that they were being well treated by the Colombian authorities.
British embassy sources in Bogota said that although the embassy was not obliged to provide interpreters, it was doing all it could to assist the Haynes and Shaw.

If the three men are convicted of drug smuggling offences, they could face between four and 12 years in prison. Sentences could be slashed in return for admissions of guilt or giving information about alleged suppliers.
